paper_metadata.title: Effect of Ti addition on the microstructure and properties of AlCrCuFeNi alloy

evidence.quote: The microstructure, hardness, compression and wear resistance of AlCrCuFeNi，AlCrCuFeNiTi0.5 and different heat treatment (600 ℃/12h,800℃/12h,1000℃/12h)annealed AlCrCuFeNiTi 0.5 High Entropy Alloys(HEAs) fabricated by arc melting and casting were investigated
After the addition of Ti,the hardness and wear resistance of AlCrCuFeNiTi0.5 alloy improves.

attributes.morphology: typical cast dendrite structure with DR-A and DR-B regions

evidence.quote: The microstructure exhibits a typical cast dendrite structure and possess similar form. Two parts of the dendrite defined as DR-A and DR-B are observed in these alloys.

attributes.morphology: typical cast dendrite structure with enlarged black spherical particles in DR-B and network-like spinodal products interdendritically

evidence.quote: With the addition of Ti, the black spherical particles in the DR-B region become larger, and the spinodal decomposition products in the interdendritic region tend to become a network structure.

attributes.morphology: spinodal decomposition products between dendrites changed into striped structures

evidence.quote: All the alloys exhibit a typical cast dendrite structure. By heating treatment, the phase in the dendritic region DR-B tends to grow in the middle of DR-A... At 600℃ , the spinodal decomposition products between dendrites changed into striped structures, and the number of nanoparticles in dendrites increased.
XRD and EDS analysis indicate that DR-A phase is NiAl-based compounds, DR-B is Cr based BCC phase and ID is Cu-rich FCC phase.

attributes.morphology: DR-B phase grows within DR-A; decreased interdendritic volume fraction

evidence.quote: All the alloys exhibit a typical cast dendrite structure. By heating treatment, the phase in the dendritic region DR-B tends to grow in the middle of DR-A, rather than separate growth of the two phases. In addition, the volume fraction between dendrites decreases with the increase of annealing temperature.

conflicts.description: Hardness of the as-cast AlCrCuFeNiTi0.5 alloy is reported as 460±2 HV in Table 2 and Table 4, while the text states hardness did not increase significantly with Ti addition but Table 2 gives 425±3 HV for Ti0; also the text claims strength/hardness improve with increasing heat-treatment temperature, yet Table 4 shows a sawtooth variation (478 HV at 600 °C, 429 HV at 800 °C) and the alloy shows best resistance to softening at 600 °C.

evidence.quote: It can be seen that the hardness of the alloy did not increase significantly with the addition of Ti.
There is no doubt that the volume wear rate and hardness of the alloy are sawtooth changes.The alloy exhibits the best resistance to high temperature softening at 600℃.

conflicts.description: The conclusion states strength, hardness, plasticity and wear resistance all improve with increasing heating temperature, but Table 4 shows wear rate increasing from 17.9 at 600 °C to 38.7 at 800 °C (worse wear resistance) and hardness decreasing from 600 to 800 °C.

evidence.quote: With the incerase of heating temperature, the strength, hardness, plasticity and wear resistance of AlCrCuFeNiTi0.5 alloy are improved.
